title: Lighthouse — handoff digest & temporary runbook (night bridge)
content:
Context:
This is a lightweight 'bridge' handoff for the night shift. We ran into recurring 95th-percentile tail latency spikes on hosted-api when sequence length > 2k tokens for the new llama2-epic variant. That variant is currently in A/B at 10% and is causing intermittent kvcache miss storms on servepool-c.

Current state (as of handoff):
- Incident level: SEV-2 (customer-visible but degraded).
- Affected routes: /v1/generate (model: llama2-epic:2026-03-10) for long-context requests only. Short requests unaffected.
- Traffic routing: 10% canary -> llama2-epic on servepool-c; fallback path configured to standard-llama2 for errors. Fallbacks have been triggered ~8 times in last 3 hours.
- Autoscaler: working; no OOMs reported on GPUs.
- Error signatures: increased 502s with message 'kvcache-miss-timeout' and tail latencies > 2.5s.
- Temporary mitigation in place: Canary paused at 5% (reduced from 10%) at 02:40 PT; TTL for pause expires at 08:00 PT unless lifted.

Immediate triage checklist (what I did during shift):
1) Confirmed metrics: SRE dashboard (Console -> latency -> route=/v1/generate) shows tail spike correlated with requests with length>2048 tokens.
   Commands/URLs checked: https://console.redwood/metrics/route/generate?range=6h, grafana panel: infra/servepool-c/kvcache.
2) Collected logs for failed requests (JQL: service:runtime AND message:kvcache-miss-timeout AND time>=-6h). Saved sample IDs: req_20260312_0171, req_20260312_0233, req_20260312_0319.
3) Increased kvcache-reserve on servepool-c to 20% (was 10%) via infra-config CLI to reduce eviction storms. Command used: infractl pool update servepool-c --kvcache-reserve=0.20 (PR: github.com/.../pr/884).
4) Reduced canary weight to 5% and set automatic rollback on error-rate>1.5% for 30m window.
5) Opened INF-4123 with notes and attached request samples.

Quick runbook (temp steps to follow if spike recurs):
- If 95p latency > 1.8s for > 15m and error-rate > 1%:
  a) Immediately reduce canary to 0% (infractl canary set --model=llama2-epic --weight=0).
  b) Increase kvcache-reserve by +10 percentage pts on affected servepool (infractl pool update servepool-c --kvcache-reserve=0.30).
  c) Toggle per-request prefix-caching: set header X-Redwood-Prefix-Cache=enable temporarily at the gateway for long-context routes.
  d) If retries are flooding origin, set retry-limit=1 on gateway for /v1/generate.
  e) Notify on-call infra-engineer (pager: Samir Rao) and on-call model ops (pager: Arjun Patel).

Commands & quick snippets (copy-paste):
- Check recent tail latencies: curl -s "https://console.redwood/api/metrics?panel=route_generate&range=1h" | jq '.'
- Grab sample logs for a request ID: infra-logs get req_20260312_0319 --output=full > /tmp/req_0319.log
- Update serving pool kvcache reserve: infractl pool update servepool-c --kvcache-reserve=0.30 --reason="night-bridge quick bump"
- Set canary weight: infractl canary set --model=llama2-epic --weight=0 --memo="rollback-night-bridge"
- Toggle gateway header for prefix caching: curl -X PATCH "https://gateway.redwood/config/routes/generate" -d '{"prefix_caching":"enable"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $GATEWAY_TOKEN"
  (Note: use console token; don't paste token into chat)

Logs & artifacts to attach when escalating:
- /tmp/req_0319.log, /tmp/req_0171.log (samples)
- Grafana screenshot: grafana.redwood/p/servepool-c/kvcache-miss-dashboard (exported PNG attached in INF-4123)
- Canary rollout history: infractl canary history --model=llama2-epic --limit=20

Escalation path (who to ping, in order):
1) On-call SRE (primary): Samir Rao (@samir) pager
2) Model Ops (primary): Arjun Patel (@arjun) pager and #model-ops
3) Serving runtime lead (if >30m unresolved): Lena Ortiz (call)
4) Product lead (if customer-facing outage >2h): Priya Menon (email + call)

Open questions / TODOs (for next-day follow-up):
- Why are kvcache misses correlated with long-request patterns specifically for llama2-epic? Hypothesis: changed kv-key sharding in the new kernel. Need reproducible test to confirm.
- Run a local reproduce harness: repo: serving-runtime/test/harness/long-context-repro. I started a job at 04:10 PT (job id: longrepro-20260312-04) — results expected in morning.
- Add targeted smoke tests in CI to hit >2k sequences on a canary VM before rolling.
- Consider adding an adaptive kvcache-reserve algorithm instead of fixed percent. Related RFC: internal/rfc/adaptive-kvcache.md (draft).

Handoff checklist (what the next shift should do in first 30 min):
- Confirm current canary weight (infractl canary get --model=llama2-epic).
- Verify kvcache metrics on servepool-c (Grafana panel).
- Check INF-4123 comments and attach any new logs to the ticket.
- Review longrepro job results and paste link in this doc.
- If canary is at 0% and stable, schedule incremental reintroduce to 2% with 10m observation windows.
- If still unstable, keep canary at 0% and block merges that touch kvshuffle until root cause analysis.

Notes to self (informal):
- Don't forget to rotate the temp agent token used for the gateway header test. Left a note in 1Password: "night-bridge temp - maya".
- Samir: the late-night logs showed a weird churn around 02:10-02:20 that lines up with autoscaler churn; possible race between cache resizing + autoscaler. Flag for follow-up with infra autoscaler team.

Draft timeline (actions taken tonight):
- 23:50: alert triggered, initial investigation started.
- 00:20: sampled failed requests and opened INF-4123.
- 01:05: increased kvcache-reserve to 20% on servepool-c.
- 02:40: reduced canary to 5% and set rollback triggers.
- 04:10: started longrepro job.

Attachments (local):
- /tmp/grafana-servepoolc-20260312.png
- /tmp/req_0319.log

Closing notes:
This doc is intentionally compact — a pocket runbook for the night bridge rather than the final RCA. Please expand INF-4123 with post-mortem details tomorrow and convert the temp steps above into a proper runbook entry under Confluence: confluence.redwood/inference/runbooks/kvcache-long-context (draft only).

If anything critical crops up, page the infra lead directly (call number in 1Password).

-- Maya C. (night bridge, SRE)
